problem.text: The workflow identifies an ongoing CUDA dependency issue. This attempt extends its existing exact-version installation workaround to libnvidia-cfg1.

reasoning.text: Requesting the same package release for libnvidia-cfg1 and nvidia-persistenced appears intended to constrain package resolution before CUDA setup; the available source does not establish the underlying dependency conflict.

impact.text: Only the guarded Linux CUDA provisioning step changes. Windows provisioning and the CUDA-empty source-distribution path retain their previous commands.

source_notes.text: Read the earlier workaround entry, which records restoring exact-version nvidia-persistenced installation and hold. It provides historical context, not proof of successful package resolution.

Whole-parent searches found no libnvidia occurrences. NVIDIA matches include workflow provisioning, calibration text and CUDA documentation references; none establishes a Python import name for this system package. Dynamic loading and external use are not ruled out.

Supplied issue #8 reports an invalid tensor reshape during model quantization. Its discussion attributes that problem to missing padding and reports subsequent success. Those reports do not verify this APT workaround.

limitations: No APT transaction, PowerShell script, GitHub Actions job or wheel build was executed; package availability and successful dependency resolution remain unverified.
The external CUDA action and linked NVIDIA forum explanation were not inspected.
The Python check counted matrix declarations; it did not execute workflow conditions or provisioning.

chapters.title: Extend the CUDA package workaround to libnvidia-cfg1

claims.text: After installing and holding nvidia-persistenced, the step now requests libnvidia-cfg1=575.57.08-0ubuntu1 using apt-get install -y --allow-downgrades, then requests apt-mark hold libnvidia-cfg1. The numeric string selects a package release, not a CUDA toolkit version. No APT preference file is added.

The new commands reuse the existing step's non-Windows/nonempty-CUDA guard and inherited pwsh shell. They follow APT repository setup and index refresh, and precede Jimver/cuda-toolkit@v0.2.25 with matrix.cuda, network installation and --toolkit. The task changes neither that action nor its inputs.
A bounded Python inspection counted nine parent matrix rows, including four Ubuntu CUDA rows covering Python 3.10–3.13. These rows request CUDA 12.8.1.

The installation and hold are coupled: installation requests the exact release first, while the following hold seeks to retain the installed package selection. This extends the existing constrained-package strategy rather than changing toolkit selection, trading flexibility for a more specific provisioning environment.

annotation.summary: Adds exact-version libnvidia-cfg1 installation and hold before Linux CUDA setup, extending the existing nvidia-persistenced workaround without establishing build success.

argv:
import pathlib,re
s=pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/build.yml').read_text()
r=re.findall(r"- \{ artname:.*",s)
linux=[x for x in r if 'os: ubuntu-' in x and "cuda: '12.8.1'" in x]
print({'matrix_rows':len(r),'linux_cuda_rows':len(linux),'python_versions':[re.search(r"pyver: '([^']+)'",x).group(1) for x in linux]})
